paragraphs: Here's what I want you to carry out of this one, friend. Job's friends have been handing him tidy answers about why he suffers, and Job isn't buying them. He points out that God's wisdom and strength are bigger than any neat formula: "Wisdom and strength belong to God; counsel and understanding are His." (Job 12:13) Even the powerful, the counselors, the judges and the kings, are in His hand, and so is "the breath of all mankind." (Job 12:10, 17-21)

So what do you do when people explain your hard season with answers that don't fit? Job doesn't pretend, and he doesn't walk away from God. He tells his friends he wants to speak to the Almighty (Job 13:3), and he says, "Though He slay me, I will hope in Him." (Job 13:15) That's a man who is hurting, honest and still leaning toward God, all in one breath, and I think that's a LOT harder than sounding wise from the couch.

Now, a warning for me and for you: Job asks his friends if they will "speak wickedly on God's behalf" (Job 13:7), and I think that should make all of us slow down before we explain what God is doing in somebody else's pain. Sometimes the wisest thing is to sit quietly with a hurting friend, like Job says: "If only you would remain silent; for that would be your wisdom!" (Job 13:5) Be honest with God, trust that wisdom and strength are His, and keep your hope where Job kept his. The story isn't over, friend, because Job still has more to say.
